sermon.title: The Amazing Bible Predicts and Influences Future History 04/29/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer argues that the Bible predicted the falling away, restoration and times of refreshing. He traces how the great awakenings shaped America’s founding, the abolition and women’s rights movements, and later revivals, then lists errors that followed: Pentecostal excesses, date-setting, faith in faith, prosperity teaching and unconditional love. He closes with Daniel 11:32: people who know God will be strong.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Garbled names are marked [unclear], including the person who took him to a restaurant (private). Kept as spoken: “Acts 3:20”; Declaration wording (“unchangeable rights”) (8:11); the Supreme Court in the “1840s” said blacks were not human; separate but equal in “1898” (24:05); “In God We Trust” put on money in the early 50s (48:33). Unverified: only 25% attend church (14:31); a papal document approving slavery (17:28); Southern Baptists founded over slavery; 23% of Americans are liberals but control 92% of education, after a 1933 manifesto (37:30); predictions by Billy Graham (1952) and others (42:51, 63:11); Trump got saved a year and a half before running (54:38); children die every year from faith healing (50:29). Sensitive content kept as spoken: gun control and the right to abolish a destructive government (9:31); liberals cut the military, people “want freebies” (12:32); RINOs (21:30); Pentecostal snake handling, women’s dress rules (“women cause men to commit adultery”) (32:12–36:23). On a minister taking a widow’s Social Security check: “I want to smack him upside the head” (51:26). Positive thinking and Trump’s pastor; prosperity preachers and “dumb Christians” (52:46–54:38); Jesus people “nonsense” (62:13).
